briefing:
SITUATION BRIEFING — Day 1, 18:00 CET

Russia has launched a military operation to seize the Suwalki Corridor, the 65km land bridge between Poland and Lithuania. In 12 hours of fighting, Russian forces from Kaliningrad have advanced approximately 25km into southern Lithuania, engaging and pushing back the German-led NATO eFP battlegroup. The corridor is now actively contested with Russian forces holding the northern section and Polish forces defending the southern approaches from Suwałki. A critical 15km zone between the lines sees ongoing skirmishes between Russian VDV airborne troops and Polish mechanized reconnaissance units.

NATO's response is mobilizing but fragmented. Poland has fully committed its 16th Mechanized Division and is moving additional forces north. The US has raised DEFCON 3 for V Corps in Europe and is deploying F-35s to Łask Air Base, but the S-400 umbrella from Kaliningrad currently prevents NATO air operations over the corridor itself. The UK has activated the Joint Expeditionary Force and dispatched HMS Queen Elizabeth carrier strike group toward the Baltic. France has deployed a Rafale squadron to Poland. However, Germany remains deeply cautious with only 22% war support, and Turkey and Hungary are blocking rapid NATO consensus on Article 5 invocation.

Russia has elevated its nuclear posture to 'dispersal' and issued a public warning that any NATO attack on Russian sovereign territory (including Kaliningrad) would be met with 'all necessary means.' Belarus forces are positioned on the Lithuanian border but have not yet crossed. A Russian Iskander missile malfunctioned and landed 3km inside Polish territory — no casualties, but technically a strike on NATO soil. Cyber attacks have intensified against Lithuanian and Polish networks, with partial disruption to Lithuanian mobile communications. Approximately 15,000 Lithuanian civilians have fled south toward Poland from the Marijampolė area, with another 8,000 heading to Latvia.

Global markets are in turmoil: oil at $108.50/barrel, European indices down 6-8%. The UN Security Council emergency session ended without resolution after Russian and Chinese vetoes. NATO's North Atlantic Council is in continuous session with Article 4 consultation underway and growing pressure for Article 5. The next 12-24 hours will be critical — Russia must consolidate its corridor gains before NATO masses sufficient forces for a counterattack.
narrative:
At 06:30 CET, Russian forces launched Operation Corridor from Kaliningrad Oblast. VDV airborne troops conducted a heliborne assault on key road junctions near Vištytis and Mockava in southern Lithuania, while the 11th Army Corps pushed mechanized columns southeast along the A7 highway toward the Suwalki Gap. The opening salvo included Iskander-M precision strikes against the German-led NATO eFP battlegroup near Marijampolė, destroying several Puma IFVs and disrupting command communications. S-400 batteries in Kaliningrad activated full engagement protocols, establishing an A2/AD bubble over the corridor that prevented NATO close air support.

The German eFP battlegroup, though on alert, was caught in a dispersed posture and suffered significant losses in the opening hours. German troops fought fiercely at Marijampolė but were forced to fall back toward Kaunas, yielding ground in the corridor. Meanwhile, Poland's 16th Mechanized Division raced north from Suwałki, establishing a blocking position along the Polish-Lithuanian border. By midday the initial Russian thrust had gained approximately 25km into the corridor before encountering stiffening Polish and German resistance.

By 18:00 CET, the situation had stabilized into a contested zone. Russia held the northern portion of the corridor near Kaliningrad, while Polish forces held the southern approaches from Suwałki. A 15km gap between the lines remained actively contested, with Russian VDV paratroopers dug in at road junctions and Polish mechanized units probing their positions. Belarus forces remained on the Lithuanian border but had not crossed — Moscow holding them in reserve as a second-echelon threat. The first NATO casualties — 14 German soldiers killed, 23 wounded — sent shockwaves through European capitals.

Global markets reacted with panic. Oil surged past $108/barrel. The euro dropped to 1.04 against the dollar. An emergency UN Security Council session was convened but produced no resolution as Russia and China blocked action. NATO held an emergency North Atlantic Council session, with Poland invoking Article 4. The Article 5 debate remained unresolved, with Hungary and Turkey raising objections, though 28 other members expressed strong solidarity. A Russian Iskander missile targeting Polish military communications near Suwałki malfunctioned and crashed in an unpopulated forest area 3km inside Polish territory — technically a Russian missile strike on Polish soil that dramatically strengthened the case for Article 5.

surprises: Lithuanian signals intelligence intercepts Russian comms revealing disagreement between VDV commander and Kaliningrad ground forces over priorities — VDV wants to push south while ground forces want to consolidate. The 4-hour pause allows Polish forces to establish stronger blocking positions.

A Russian Iskander missile targeting Polish military comms near Suwałki malfunctions and crashes 3km inside Polish territory. No casualties, but this is technically a Russian strike on Polish soil — dramatically strengthening the Article 5 case.
